watches.name: Arsenale Moissanite - 6121514C
watches.description: For centuries, Venice stood as one of the world’s foremost crossroads for gemstones, craftsmanship, and decorative arts. Precious stones from distant lands flowed through the Serenissima, nurturing a tradition shaped by fine workmanship, intricate gem-setting, and the pursuit of light as a form of artistic expression. watches.description: The Redentore HK Limited Edition was born from the collaboration between Venezianico and Horoverse, combining Venetian elegance with the historical memory of Hong Kong. Inspired by the legendary “Dukling” junk boat, the dial reinterprets the city’s early colonial map through flowing lines and three-dimensional details, creating a dialogue between two waterfront cities deeply connected to their maritime identity. The metallic relief of the Dukling appears to sail across the natural mother-of-pearl dial, while the engraved caseback pays tribute to the historic Star Ferry Pier and Hong Kong’s harbour heritage. Each edition embodies a different spirit of the city: The Tide (浪濤), The Shore (泊岸), and The Soul (赤誠), the latter strictly limited to only 10 pieces worldwide. watches.name: Nereide Verdigris - 4521549
watches.description: Venice is a city shaped by time. The lagoon’s water, salty air, and humidity slowly transform the metals of its architecture. On domes, statues, and decorative surfaces in copper and brass, a green-turquoise patina known as verdigris gradually forms, becoming one of the most recognizable tones of the Venetian landscape. The dial of Nereide Verdigris draws inspiration from this transformation. Made of brass, it undergoes a controlled oxidation process that develops the characteristic patina, creating shades that shift between green, turquoise, and blue. Each dial is slightly different, echoing the colors of Venetian metals shaped by time and the lagoon.

watches.name: Nereide Chimera - Limited Edition
watches.description: Nereide Chimera explores the idea of union through material. Its dial is made of Iron Tiger, a composite stone formed by Tiger’s Eye, Red Jasper, and Hematite, where different minerals merge into a single surface defined by natural stratifications and visual depth. The name Chimera refers to this material union and to a broader cultural reference rooted in Venice. The winged lion, emblem of the city, is itself a chimera: a figure composed of different natures unified into a single form. In the same way, Iron Tiger brings together distinct minerals into a single material expression.
